Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Mining | National Government to sustain quarterly engagements with mining industry – Deputy Lands Minister Source : Emmanuel Tetteh 28 November 2026 9:51am ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources has reaffirmed its commitment to holding quarterly engagements with the mining industry to strengthen collaboration, address concerns and build consensus on issues affecting the sector.
The Deputy Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Dr Yusif Sulemana, speaking on behalf of the sector Minister, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, said the engagements initiated this year would be sustained to promote constructive dialogue between the government, mining companies and relevant institutions.
Speaking at the 12th Ghana Mining Industry Awards in Accra on Friday, November 27, Dr Sulemana urged the Ghana Chamber of Mines and its members to maintain open and constructive engagements with the ministry and other relevant public institutions.
He said although stakeholders might not always agree on every issue, they must remain willing to listen to different perspectives, examine the available evidence and work towards mutually acceptable solutions.
“I therefore encourage the Chamber and its members to continue engaging openly and constructively with my ministry and the rest of the relevant institutions. This is the reason why I intend to continue the quarterly engagements we started this year,” he said.
Dr Sulemana explained that the ministry had already held quarterly consultations with stakeholders and was committed to maintaining the arrangement in the coming years.
He stressed that differences in opinion should not prevent stakeholders from working together, particularly where decisions have implications for the long-term development of Ghana's mineral resources.
“We may not agree on every issue, but we must always be willing to listen to each other, examine the evidence and work towards solutions that serve Ghana's long-term interest,” he added.
The Deputy Minister emphasised that sustained engagement and consensus-building were essential to resolving disagreements and strengthening relations between government and industry players.
He said the willingness of stakeholders to engage and reach common ground would be critical to advancing the country's mining sector.
The 12th Ghana Mining Industry Awards brought together key stakeholders to celebrate excellence and recognise contributions to Ghana's mining industry.
